sanskrit.deva:
ॐ आप्यायन्तु ममाङ्गानि वाक्प्राणश्चक्षुः श्रोत्रमथो बलमिन्द्रियाणि च सर्वाणि ।
सर्वं ब्रह्मौपनिषदं माहं ब्रह्म निराकुर्यां मा मा ब्रह्म निराकरोदनिराकरणमस्त्वनिराकरणं मेऽस्तु ।
तदात्मनि निरते य उपनिषत्सु धर्मास्ते मयि सन्तु ते मयि सन्तु ॥
ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥

grammar.en: past passive participle m. loc. sg.

closing.translation: Om. May my limbs grow strong: speech, prāṇa, eye, ear, strength, and all the senses. All is the Brahman of the Upaniṣads. May I not reject Brahman; may Brahman not reject me. Let there be no rejecting; let there be no rejecting on my part. May the dharmas taught in the Upaniṣads be in me, who delight in that Self; may they be in me. Om. Peace, peace, peace.
notes: The peace invocation of the Upaniṣads of the Sāmaveda, printed in a frame before the Kenopaniṣad in the 1910 edition (vol. 4, scan leaf 50) and again before and after the vākya-bhāṣya. Śaṅkara's bhāṣya does not comment on it; the translation gives the plain sense of the words.

sanskrit.deva:
ब्रह्मेति होवाच ब्रह्मणो वा एतद्विजये महीयध्वमिति ।
ततो हैव विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
brahmeti hovāca brahmaṇo vā etad vijaye mahīyadhvam iti |
tato haiva vidāṃcakāra brahmeti || 1 ||

lines.iast: brahmeti hovāca brahmaṇo vā etad vijaye mahīyadhvam iti
lines.deva: ब्रह्मेति होवाच ब्रह्मणो वा एतद्विजये महीयध्वमिति

padaccheda.iast: brahma iti ha uvāca brahmaṇaḥ vai etat vijaye mahīyadhvam iti tataḥ ha eva vidāṃcakāra brahma iti
padaccheda.deva: ब्रह्म इति ह उवाच ब्रह्मणः वै एतत् विजये महीयध्वम् इति ततः ह एव विदांचकार ब्रह्म इति

translations.text: ‘It is Brahman’, she said. ‘It is in Brahman's victory that you attain greatness thus.’ From that alone he knew that it was Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara: in the victory of the Lord alone: the asuras were conquered by the Lord, and you were only the occasion; in his victory you attain greatness. etat qualifies the verb. Your conceit, ‘ours alone is this victory, ours alone this greatness’, was false. tato ha eva: from Umā's words alone Indra knew it to be Brahman; the stress shows that it was not by himself.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्माद्वा एते देवा अतितरामिवान्यान्देवान्यदग्निर्वायुरिन्द्रः ।
ते ह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्शुस्ते ह्येनत्प्रथमो विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmād vā ete devā atitarām ivānyān devān yad agnir vāyur indraḥ |
te hy enan nediṣṭhaṃ pasparśus te hy enat prathamo vidāṃcakāra brahmeti || 2 ||

lines.iast: tasmād vā ete devā atitarām ivānyān devān yad agnir vāyur indraḥ
te hy enan nediṣṭhaṃ pasparśus te hy enat prathamo vidāṃcakāra brahmeti
lines.deva: ते ह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्शुस्ते ह्येनत्प्रथमो विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति

padaccheda.iast: tasmāt vai ete devāḥ atitarām iva anyān devān yat agniḥ vāyuḥ indraḥ te hi enat nediṣṭham pasparśuḥ te hi enat prathamaḥ vidāṃcakāra brahma iti
padaccheda.deva: तस्मात् वै एते देवाः अतितराम् इव अन्यान् देवान् यत् अग्निः वायुः इन्द्रः ते हि एनत् नेदिष्ठम् पस्पर्शुः ते हि एनत् प्रथमः विदांचकार ब्रह्म इति

translations.text: Therefore these gods, Agni, Vāyu and Indra, surpass, as it were, the other gods; for they touched it nearest, and they were the first to know it as Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara: because these gods came near to Brahman, by speaking with it, seeing it and so on, they surpass the other gods in power, quality and great good fortune. iva has no sense here, or is for emphasis. nediṣṭham: nearest, dearest. prathamaḥ stands for the plural, ‘being the foremost’, and vidāṃcakāra for vidāṃcakruḥ.
The number of this mantra is not printed in the edition (the mantra ends with a bare double daṇḍa); the mantras before and after it are numbered 1 and 3.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्माद्वा इन्द्रोऽतितरामिवान्यान्देवान् ।
स ह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्श स ह्येनत्प्रथमो विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmād vā indro 'titarām ivānyān devān |
sa hy enan nediṣṭhaṃ pasparśa sa hy enat prathamo vidāṃcakāra brahmeti || 3 ||

lines.iast: sa hy enan nediṣṭhaṃ pasparśa sa hy enat prathamo vidāṃcakāra brahmeti
lines.deva: स ह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्श स ह्येनत्प्रथमो विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति

padaccheda.iast: tasmāt vai indraḥ atitarām iva anyān devān saḥ hi enat nediṣṭham pasparśa saḥ hi enat prathamaḥ vidāṃcakāra brahma iti
padaccheda.deva: तस्मात् वै इन्द्रः अतितराम् इव अन्यान् देवान् सः हि एनत् नेदिष्ठम् पस्पर्श सः हि एनत् प्रथमः विदांचकार ब्रह्म इति

translations.text: Therefore Indra surpasses, as it were, the other gods; for he touched it nearest, and he was the first to know it as Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara: because even Agni and Vāyu came to know it only from Indra's words, and it was Indra who first heard from Umā's words that it was Brahman.

sanskrit.iast: tasyaiṣa ādeśo yad etad vidyuto vyadyutad ā3 itīn nyamīmiṣad ā3 ity adhidaivatam || 4 ||

lines.iast: tasyaiṣa ādeśo yad etad vidyuto vyadyutad ā3 itīn nyamīmiṣad ā3 ity adhidaivatam

padaccheda.iast: tasya eṣaḥ ādeśaḥ yat etat vidyutaḥ vyadyutat ā iti it nyamīmiṣat ā iti adhidaivatam
padaccheda.deva: तस्य एषः आदेशः यत् एतत् विद्युतः व्यद्युतत् आ इति इत् न्यमीमिषत् आ इति अधिदैवतम्

translations.text: This is the teaching of it (by a likeness): it is like this flashing of lightning; and it is like the winking (of the eye). This is with regard to the gods.

notes: Śaṅkara: ādeśa is teaching by a likeness: the likeness by which Brahman, which has no like, is taught. ‘Of lightning … has flashed’ does not construe, so it is taken as ‘the flashing of lightning’. ā has the sense of likeness: like the flashing of lightning (so ‘like a single flash of lightning’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.3.6); for Brahman showed itself once to the gods, like lightning, and vanished. Or ‘the light’ is to be supplied: the light of lightning flashed once, as it were. iti points back to the teaching: ‘this is the teaching’. it means ‘and’: here is another teaching of it. nyamīmiṣat: winked, as the eye does; the causative has the sense of the simple verb, and ā again marks the likeness: like the eye's showing and hiding with regard to its object. adhidaivatam: this is the showing of a likeness for Brahman in what concerns the deities.
The lengthened (pluta) ā is printed ā3 in the edition.

sanskrit.deva: अथाध्यात्मं यदेतद्गच्छतीव च मनोऽनेन चैतदुपस्मरत्यभीक्ष्णं संकल्पः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast: athādhyātmaṃ yad etad gacchatīva ca mano 'nena caitad upasmaraty abhīkṣṇaṃ saṃkalpaḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: athādhyātmaṃ yad etad gacchatīva ca mano 'nena caitad upasmaraty abhīkṣṇaṃ saṃkalpaḥ
lines.deva: अथाध्यात्मं यदेतद्गच्छतीव च मनोऽनेन चैतदुपस्मरत्यभीक्ष्णं संकल्पः

padaccheda.iast: atha adhyātmam yat etat gacchati iva ca manaḥ anena ca etat upasmarati abhīkṣṇam saṃkalpaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अथ अध्यात्मम् यत् एतत् गच्छति इव च मनः अनेन च एतत् उपस्मरति अभीक्ष्णम् संकल्पः

translations.text: Now with regard to the self: that the mind, as it were, goes to this (Brahman); that by it (the seeker) constantly remembers this; and (the mind's) intention (toward it).

notes: Śaṅkara: next the teaching in what concerns the inner self. The mind, as it were, approaches this Brahman, makes it an object; by this mind the seeker remembers Brahman closely and intensely; and there is the mind's intention with Brahman for its object. Since Brahman has the mind for its adjunct, it is manifested by the cognitions of the mind, intention, memory and the like, as if it were being made an object. That is the teaching of Brahman with regard to the self. With regard to the gods it is of the nature of a swift showing, like lightning and winking; with regard to the self it is manifested together with the cognitions of the mind. Taught so, Brahman can be reached by those of slow understanding, who cannot grasp Brahman without any adjunct.

sanskrit.deva:
तद्ध तद्वनं नाम तद्वनमित्युपासितव्यम् ।
स य एतदेवं वेदाभि हैनं सर्वाणि भूतानि संवाञ्छन्ति ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad dha tadvanaṃ nāma tadvanam ity upāsitavyam |
sa ya etad evaṃ vedābhi hainaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni saṃvāñchanti || 6 ||

lines.iast: tad dha tadvanaṃ nāma tadvanam ity upāsitavyam
sa ya etad evaṃ vedābhi hainaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni saṃvāñchanti
lines.deva: स य एतदेवं वेदाभि हैनं सर्वाणि भूतानि संवाञ्छन्ति

padaccheda.iast: tat ha tat-vanam nāma tat-vanam iti upāsitavyam saḥ yaḥ etat evam veda abhi ha enam sarvāṇi bhūtāni saṃvāñchanti
padaccheda.deva: तत् ह तत्-वनम् नाम तत्-वनम् इति उपासितव्यम् सः यः एतत् एवम् वेद अभि ह एनम् सर्वाणि भूतानि संवाञ्छन्ति

translations.text: That (Brahman) is called Tadvana, what is dear to all; it is to be meditated on as Tadvana. All beings long for him who knows it thus.

notes: Śaṅkara: tadvana is tasya vanam: being the inner self of the whole host of living beings, it is what they are to desire and resort to. Since Brahman is known as Tadvana, it is to be meditated on by this very name, which states its quality. The fruit of meditating by this name: all beings pray to that meditator, as they do to Brahman.

sanskrit.deva:
उपनिषदं भो ब्रूहीत्युक्ता त उपनिषत् ।
ब्राह्मीं वाव त उपनिषदमब्रूमेति ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
upaniṣadaṃ bho brūhīty uktā ta upaniṣat |
brāhmīṃ vāva ta upaniṣadam abrūmeti || 7 ||

lines.iast: upaniṣadaṃ bho brūhīty uktā ta upaniṣat

padaccheda.iast: upaniṣadam bhoḥ brūhi iti uktā te upaniṣat brāhmīm vāva te upaniṣadam abrūma iti
padaccheda.deva: उपनिषदम् भोः ब्रूहि इति उक्ता ते उपनिषत् ब्राह्मीम् वाव ते उपनिषदम् अब्रूम इति

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: (The pupil:) ‘Sir, tell me the Upaniṣad.’ (The teacher:) ‘The Upaniṣad has been told to you; we have indeed told you the Upaniṣad concerning Brahman.’

notes: Śaṅkara: upaniṣad: the secret that is to be reflected on. brāhmī: of Brahman, the supreme Self, for the knowledge taught above has the supreme Self for its subject. ‘We have told’ confirms that the Upaniṣad already given is the one concerning the supreme Self, with a view to what follows.

Śaṅkara, on the pupil's question: what does one who has heard the Upaniṣad mean by asking for it? If he asks about what he has heard, the question is a useless repetition, like grinding what is ground. If the Upaniṣad had been told with something left over, it would not have been closed with the statement of its fruit (2.5); so the question is not about a remainder either. His meaning is this: does the Upaniṣad already told need some further means, as a part of it or as a help to it, or does it need nothing? If it needs something, tell me the Upaniṣad about that; if it needs nothing, confirm it, as Pippalāda did, ‘there is nothing beyond this’ (Praśna 6.7). So the teacher's confirmation, ‘the Upaniṣad has been told to you’, fits.

Śaṅkara, on the same: it may be said that this is no confirmation, since he goes on to say more (4.8). Something more is said, but not as a part of the Upaniṣad or as a means that works with it; it is said as the way to attain the knowledge of Brahman, for austerity and the rest are put on a level with the Vedas and their limbs by being named together with them, and the Vedas and their limbs cannot be parts of the knowledge of Brahman or work together with it. May not things named together be applied apart, as each fits, as the mantras of the sūktavāka are divided according to their deities: austerity, restraint, rites and truth as parts of the knowledge or helps to it, the Vedas and their limbs, which make meanings known, as means to rites and to the knowledge of the Self? No: the division does not hold. The knowledge of Brahman, which sets aside every notion of the difference of act, means and fruit, cannot need a part or be joined to a helping means; it and its fruit, the highest good, rest in the inner Self, turned away from every object. So action cannot work together with knowledge, nor knowledge need action as a part. The question and answer are therefore for confirmation: this much is the Upaniṣad, and it needs nothing else for immortality.

sanskrit.deva: तस्यै तपो दमः कर्मेति प्रतिष्ठा वेदाः सर्वाङ्गानि सत्यमायतनम् ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast: tasyai tapo damaḥ karmeti pratiṣṭhā vedāḥ sarvāṅgāni satyam āyatanam || 8 ||

lines.iast: tasyai tapo damaḥ karmeti pratiṣṭhā vedāḥ sarvāṅgāni satyam āyatanam
lines.deva: तस्यै तपो दमः कर्मेति प्रतिष्ठा वेदाः सर्वाङ्गानि सत्यमायतनम्

padaccheda.iast: tasyai tapaḥ damaḥ karma iti pratiṣṭhā vedāḥ sarva-aṅgāni satyam āyatanam
padaccheda.deva: तस्यै तपः दमः कर्म इति प्रतिष्ठा वेदाः सर्व-अङ्गानि सत्यम् आयतनम्

translations.text: Austerity, restraint, rites (and the like) are its footing, (and so are) the Vedas and all their limbs; truth is its abode.

notes: Śaṅkara: tasyai: of the Upaniṣad concerning Brahman just spoken of; austerity and the rest are the means of attaining it. tapas: the collecting of body, senses and mind. dama: quieting. karma: the agnihotra and other rites. Knowledge of the truth is seen to arise, through purity of mind, in one refined by these; and one whose stain is not rubbed away is seen not to understand, or to understand wrongly, even when Brahman is taught, as Indra and Virocana. So knowledge arises, as it is taught, in one whose mind has been purified by austerity and the rest, here or in many past births (Śvetāśvatara 6.23; Mahābhārata, Śāntiparvan 204.8). iti shows that these stand for others too that help knowledge to arise, such as humility and freedom from pretence (Gītā 13.7). pratiṣṭhā: its two feet, as it were; when these are there the knowledge of Brahman stands firm and goes forward, as a man on his feet.

Śaṅkara: the four Vedas and all the six limbs, phonetics and the rest, are also its footing, the Vedas because they make rites and knowledge known, the limbs because they guard the Vedas. Or, since pratiṣṭhā pictures the feet, the Vedas are all its other limbs, the head and the rest; on this view phonetics and the rest are included in the word ‘Vedas’. satyam: freedom from deceit, straightness of speech, mind and body. āyatanam: where the Upaniṣad dwells; knowledge rests in those who are without deceit and good, not in the deceitful, whose nature is demonic (Praśna 1.16). Truth is already included in the footing with austerity and the rest; it is named again as the abode to show that it is a means above the others (‘a thousand horse sacrifices and truth were weighed in the balance; truth alone outweighs the thousand’).

sanskrit.deva: यो वा एतामेवं वेदापहत्य पाप्मानमनन्ते स्वर्गे लोके ज्येये प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast: yo vā etām evaṃ vedāpahatya pāpmānam anante svarge loke jyeye pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati || 9 ||

lines.iast: yo vā etām evaṃ vedāpahatya pāpmānam anante svarge loke jyeye pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati
lines.deva: यो वा एतामेवं वेदापहत्य पाप्मानमनन्ते स्वर्गे लोके ज्येये प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ vai etām evam veda apahatya pāpmānam anante svarge loke jyeye pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati
padaccheda.deva: यः वै एताम् एवम् वेद अपहत्य पाप्मानम् अनन्ते स्वर्गे लोके ज्येये प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति

translations.text: He who knows this (knowledge) thus, having struck off evil, is established in the endless, the highest, world of bliss (Brahman); he is established.

notes: Śaṅkara: this knowledge of Brahman, taught from keneṣitam onward and praised by the story beginning ‘Brahman won a victory for the gods’, the ground of all knowledge. The fruit of the knowledge, though stated at 2.4, is summed up at the end. pāpman: the seed of the round of birth and death, which is ignorance, desire and action. svarge loke: in Brahman, whose nature is happiness. Because it is called endless it is not heaven; and lest ‘endless’ be taken there in a secondary sense, the mantra adds jyeye: in what is greater than all, his own Self, in the primary sense. He is established there: he does not come again to the round of birth and death.
